take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only for access, dialect or stance, and give the synthesizer a framework so it picks one diagnosis.
Handoffs are where it breaks. Audit the seams, and write what you learn into CLAUDE.md so it stays.
The audit checks how work was handed over, not whether the briefing is true. I still verify that myself.

monday.move: Rerun the pilot-cohort brief on the usage-pricing decision with the three retrievers (wiki, docs, internet) and a synthesizer using the strategy kernel. Flag where my sources contradict each other.
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team of fourteen
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: If the synthesis is just a beige summary with no committed diagnosis, or I can't trace a number back to a file, I stop and send the old brief.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: The fix for a stuck agent was often files, a framework, a split of roles or a rule in CLAUDE.md, not a better prompt. The 'one good prompt' slides pull the other way, so it's shaken, not changed.

one_line: Good hands-on hour with real sources, but the 'don't split' point got made four times and I still can't tell whether the answer is true.
